content.text: No customer-payable liquidated damages, penalties, or early-termination/minimum fees exist anywhere in the agreement.

input.quote: Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no liquidated damages, penalty, cancellation charge or minimum/early-termination fee on Sparkling. Section 11 obliges Sparkling only to pay the fees set out in the Fee Schedule, and Section 17(b) gives Sparkling an unqualified right to terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice with no termination payment or stipulated damages. Section 15 confines each party's remedy to direct damages and excludes indirect/consequential damages, and there is no interest-on-late-payment or stipulated-damages mechanic. Where the Agreement does address termination for Garman's default (p0128), the money flows to us (fee refund and conversion to a perpetual royalty-free licence), which is favourable and not flagged. This meets the preferred position — no liquidated damages or penalties payable by the Customer — so no redline is proposed.
